physics_goals.quote: Here we report Q_W^p=0.0719+-0.0045, as extracted from our measured parity-violating (PV) polarized electron-proton scattering asymmetry
physics_goals.value: Measure the proton's weak charge through the parity-violating asymmetry in polarised electron-proton scattering, a low-energy test of the Standard Model

summary.plain: Qweak measured how electrons spinning one way versus the other scatter differently from protons in a hydrogen target at Jefferson Lab. That tiny asymmetry gave the proton's weak charge, a precision test of the Standard Model, which came out in agreement with it.
summary.technical: Parity-violating elastic e-p scattering at Q^2 = 0.025 (GeV/c)^2 with a 1.155 GeV, 89% longitudinally polarised, 145 microamp electron beam on a 34.4 cm liquid-hydrogen target in Hall C; final asymmetry -226.5 ± 9.3 ppb giving the proton weak charge Q_W^p = 0.0719 ± 0.0045, in agreement with the Standard Model and constraining semi-leptonic parity-violating new physics at multi-TeV scales.
